findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? so it is never used
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers in this codebase gates attributes with methods named `include_<attr>?`, as seen in include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_stats? and the methods generated by untrusted_attributes. The new method is defined as `include_website_name` without `?`, so the serializer will never call it. Consequently website_name is serialized even when website is blank (as a nil value), and the intended present? check provides no protection; the method must be renamed to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name is not hidden for untrusted TL0 users viewed anonymously
findings.body: `website` is listed in untrusted_attributes so it is suppressed when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) applies (TL0 user seen by anonymous, to prevent spam/abuse harvesting), but the newly added `website_name` attribute at line 43 is not added to that list (lines 105-111) and has no equivalent restriction check. Anonymous visitors therefore still receive the website host and, for same-domain sites, the full path derived directly from the hidden website field, defeating the existing restriction. website_name should be added to untrusted_attributes (or otherwise gated the same way), and the spec's untrusted_attributes list should cover it.

findings.title: Displayed website_name drops query string and fragment, so 'complete URL' text can be incomplete/misleading
findings.body: When the website host matches the instance host, the code returns `website_host + URI(website).path` only. For a website such as http://example.com/?page=user or http://example.com/profile#section the display text becomes just `example.com/` / `example.com/profile`, omitting the query/fragment that distinguish the actual target while the link still points to the full URL. The visible label therefore does not show the complete URL as the PR title promises; query (and fragment) should be appended when present.
